code_written_limitations: Unallocated complaints (computed by code from `area_rollup.json`): 29.7% (A19) of complaint and cancellation records (27137 (A01)) are general/unspecified: generic criticism (for example "worst update") that names no specific area, so they are not allocated to any of the four decision areas. If many of them refer to one area's problem, for example the same free-tier change, that area's total is understated; the labels cannot show which area that would be.

Premium-only boundary, upper-bound sensitivity (computed by code; `analysis/premium_only_sensitivity.json`): 2456 (T56) of the 15763 (C05) `billing.premium_only` complaint and cancellation records contain no Premium or payment word (premium, subscri-, pay/paid/paying, free, buy, money, trial, $; case-insensitive), with a severity sum of 7283 (T57). If none of them belonged to billing/support, its severity sum would fall from 52551 (A08) to 45268 (T58), below usability 52983 (A05) and playback/performance 48060 (A11). This is an upper bound, not a relabelling: many of these reviews plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle), and they were not moved to any other area.
mandatory_limitations: Counts describe the labeled reviews in the declared analysis scope of 200,013 reviews (analysis_200k.csv, a deterministic uniform sample of the 660,622-review corpus plus every empty-text row): self-selected public app reviews, not a customer population. They carry no revenue, plan tier or confirmed cancellations, so revenue at risk cannot be computed.
Cancellation language is expressed intent, not observed churn; nothing here estimates a causal effect on retention.
Star ratings and helpful votes were not used to classify; severity is judged from the text under the shared rubric.
17828 completed records are flagged needs_review, 13 are quarantined and 0 are unfinished.
The analysis covers a uniform random sample of the corpus, not every review; shares carry sampling error (intervals shown) and the 460,609 out-of-scope reviews were ingested but not classified.

alternatives.why_not_first: Billing/support's severity sum {A08} is close to but below usability's {A05}, and while its share of reviews grew the most among the four decision areas (from {T10} to {T11}, change {T12}) and its top issue is premium-only restrictions (severity sum {C06} across {C05} reviews), that issue is a free-tier packaging and entitlement policy question, not usability's core listening-experience defects, and the enricher-sample robustness check ({T42} vs {T43}) is a small-sample difference that does not override the full-dataset severity-sum lead.

Playback/performance's severity sum {A11} trails usability's {A05}, and its share of reviews actually fell from {T13} to {T14} (change {T15}) over the same months one year apart, even though the verifier's labels alone put it first on severity sum ({T46}).

Access/onboarding has by far the smallest severity sum ({A17}) and share of complaints ({T28}, interval {T29} to {T30}) among the four decision areas, despite a modest rise in share of reviews from {T07} to {T08} (change {T09}).

limitations: The verifier's disagreement on which area leads (playback/performance under its labels versus usability/billing under enricher labels) means the ranking among the top areas is not firmly settled and should be treated as provisional.

The one-year share-of-reviews comparison is a descriptive pattern in self-selected reviews and cannot establish that usability issues are causing the underlying shift, only that billing/support's share grew fastest among the four decision areas while usability's declined.
Spike-month lifts (for example {T38}, {T39}, {T40}) describe single months against a median and do not by themselves indicate whether usability's issues are trending up or down outside those months.
next_quarter_actions: Test reduced ad frequency or improved ad placement to address ad interruptions (severity sum {C10} across {C09} reviews); success would show a drop in this issue's complaint count and severity sum.
Audit and fix shuffle/repeat/queue logic to address library malfunctions (severity sum {C18} across {C17} reviews); success would show a drop in this issue's complaint count and severity sum.

Simplify navigation and clarify redesign changes to address layout complaints (severity sum {C30} across {C29} reviews); success would show a drop in this issue's complaint count and share of complaints.

As a hedge, review premium-only restriction messaging and free-tier entitlement communication (severity sum {C06} across {C05} reviews), given billing/support's fastest-growing share of reviews ({T12}); success would show this issue's share of reviews stop rising in the following year's comparison.
rationale: Usability's severity sum {A05} is the highest among the four decision areas, narrowly ahead of billing/support's severity sum {A08}, with playback/performance at {A11} and access/onboarding at {A17}; its three largest issues (ads {C10}, library/queue {C18}, navigation {C30}) together account for most of that total.

Usability's share of complaints {T19} (interval {T20} to {T21}) does not overlap with billing/support's share of complaints {T22} (interval {T23} to {T24}), so usability's share of complaints is higher within sampling error.

Over the same months one year apart, usability's share of reviews fell from {T16} to {T17} (change {T18}), while billing/support's share rose from {T10} to {T11} (change {T12}), the largest increase among the four decision areas; this growth trend is a reason to monitor billing/support closely even though it does not overturn usability's higher baseline severity sum.

The independent verifier, applied to a sample of {T41} reviews, orders decision areas differently: under verifier labels playback/performance leads on severity sum ({T46}), with usability second ({T47}) still ahead of billing/support ({T48}); under the enricher's own labels for that same sample, billing/support ({T42}) edges ahead of usability ({T43}). This is a labelling disagreement on a small sample, and it makes the recommendation provisional rather than a reason to depart from the full-dataset leader.

Usability also shows a lift during the spike month {T35}, where shuffle/repeat (usability.library) showed a lift of {T40}, alongside larger lifts for premium-only restrictions ({T38}) and general complaints ({T39}).
output.recommendation: Usability carries the highest baseline severity sum of the four decision areas, severity sum {A05} across its complaint and cancellation reviews, driven chiefly by ad interruptions (severity sum {C10} across {C09} reviews, mean severity {C11}), shuffle/repeat/queue malfunctions (severity sum {C18} across {C17} reviews, mean severity {C19}), and navigation/layout complaints after redesigns (severity sum {C30} across {C29} reviews, mean severity {C31}). This is core listening-experience and interface work: reducing ad frequency/placement, fixing shuffle and repeat logic, and simplifying navigation, not a payment or billing defect.
what_would_change_the_call: A larger verified sample confirming the verifier's severity-sum ordering ({T46}, {T47}, {T48}) rather than the current small-sample disagreement with enricher labels ({T42}, {T43}) would weaken confidence in usability's lead.

If billing/support's share-of-reviews growth (from {T10} to {T11}, change {T12}) continues into the following year's same-months comparison and overtakes usability's share, that would favor billing/support instead.

A human audit of the premium-only records without a payment word (upper-bound sensitivity on {T56}, severity sum {T57}) finding most are genuinely about free-tier restrictions rather than mislabeled would strengthen billing/support's case relative to usability.

payload.question: Where should the next quarter of product-improvement effort go: access/onboarding, usability, playback/performance, or billing/support?

top_issues.definition: General praise or criticism with no specific feature, unrelated content (politics, artists, boycotts), or meaningless text.
top_issues.name: General or unrelated

top_issues.definition: Features locked to Premium: skip limits, forced shuffle, cannot pick songs, cannot repeat or rewind, lyrics or offline behind a paywall, 'everything needs Premium now'.
top_issues.name: Premium-only restrictions
top_issues.summary: Free users report losing basic playback controls like song selection, skipping, repeat, and offline access unless they pay for Premium.

top_issues.definition: Too many, too long, too loud or repeated ads; ads interrupting listening.
top_issues.name: Ad interruptions
top_issues.summary: Customers report frequent, repeated ad breaks interrupting music listening, making the app frustrating to use.

top_issues.definition: Music stops, pauses, skips by itself, will not start, or plays the wrong song.
top_issues.name: Playback stops or skips
top_issues.summary: Customers report that playback randomly pauses, stops, or plays the wrong song, disrupting their listening experience.

top_issues.definition: Managing the queue, playlists, liked songs or library; shuffle or repeat controls that misbehave.
top_issues.name: Shuffle, repeat and queue malfunctions
top_issues.summary: Customers report that shuffle, repeat, queue, and playlist playback behave unpredictably, playing wrong or repeated songs and disrupting intended listening order.

top_issues.definition: App crashes, freezes, will not open or load, blank screens.
top_issues.name: App crashes, freezes, and fails to load
top_issues.summary: Customers report the app freezes, crashes, or gets stuck loading, often requiring force-stops or reinstalls without resolving the issue.

top_issues.definition: Cannot log in, keeps getting logged out, login or verification-code errors.
top_issues.name: Login and verification failures
top_issues.summary: Customers are unexpectedly logged out or cannot log back in due to failed verification codes, phone number errors, or connection issues, disrupting their listening.

top_issues.definition: Hard to find things, confusing layout, redesigns or home-screen changes, buttons moved or removed.
top_issues.name: Navigation and layout
top_issues.summary: Customers find the redesigned interface confusing and cluttered, making it hard to locate music and features quickly.

top_issues.definition: Recommendations, the algorithm, autoplay or radio picks, the DJ, unwanted suggested songs.
top_issues.name: Unwanted song insertions in playlists/radio
top_issues.summary: Customers report that the app's algorithm inserts repeated or unwanted songs and podcasts into playlists and radio, disrupting their intended listening experience.

top_issues.definition: Songs, artists, albums or podcasts missing, removed, greyed out or unavailable.
top_issues.name: Missing or removed content
top_issues.summary: Customers find that specific songs, albums, or artist catalogs are unavailable, blocked, or removed, preventing them from listening to desired content.

period_comparison.comparison_scope: areas lists the four decision areas only; areas that are not decision options are under non_decision_areas
period_comparison.method: share = complaint/cancellation reviews in the area / all classified reviews in the period; Wilson 95% intervals; identical calendar months one year apart avoid the partial first/last months and seasonal mix. Descriptive only: reviews are self-selected, not a customer census.

premium_only_sensitivity.interpretation: Upper-bound sensitivity, not a relabelling. It assumes that none of the records without a Premium or payment word belongs in billing/support and adds them to no other area. Many of them plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle, no repeat or rewind), and non-English payment words (for example 'paisa') are not matched, so the real effect is smaller than shown.
premium_only_sensitivity.what: upper-bound sensitivity of the billing/support lead to the premium-only topic boundary, computed by code; not a relabelling

spike_months.measure: the issue's complaint and cancellation reviews as a share of all reviews in the month, minus the same share in the other full months (share of reviews)
the issue's complaint and cancellation reviews as a share of all reviews in the month, minus the same share in the other full months (share of reviews)

verifier_robustness.metric: severity_sum (the baseline priority) over complaint and cancellation reviews, row-weighted

top_by_complaint_count.note: area names only, no counts: state in words, cite no token

unallocated_complaints.what: complaint and cancellation records labelled with no specific area (generic criticism); not allocated to any decision area
